# Dockerfile and Containerfile counters, for a rule with the prompt file-body-ops: one per line,
# label TAB pattern (Java regex). The [ignore] line blanks comment lines (a # at the start of a line,
# after blanks; a parser directive such as "# syntax=" is a comment too), the body of a BuildKit
# heredoc (RUN <<EOF, COPY <<-"CONF" /etc/app.conf: the rest of the instruction's line and every line
# up to the one that holds only the marker, that line too; never closed, it runs to the end of the
# file) and the lines a backslash at the end of a line continues, with the comment and empty lines
# among them, as Docker reads them. A heredoc opens only at a word that starts with << (after a
# blank; not <<<) of a RUN, COPY or ADD instruction, on its line (within its first 1,000
# characters) or on a line it continues, so a shift (1<<x) or a << in a LABEL or ENV value opens
# none. An instruction counts at the start of a line, in any case, so a
# word in a RUN command continued over lines or in a heredoc does not, not even an env or a from that
# starts a continued line.
# "build stages" counts every FROM; "environment entries" an ENV or ARG instruction, not each name
# of one. OpsFactPatternsTest pins every case; ProfileFactPatternsLinearityTest measures that
# every pattern reads linearly.
[ignore] comments and continued lines
build stages
RUN instructions
COPY and ADD instructions
environment entries
exposed ports
users
entrypoints and commands
healthchecks
